documents.unit: Student Handbook / Honor Code (Educational Policy Committee statement on AI)
documents.title: The Honor Code (incl. EPC Policy Statement on AI and Generative AI Statements)
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); AI provision in force since Fall 2023
documents.summary: The Honor Code page embeds the faculty-passed Educational Policy Committee statement: unauthorized AI use in submitted coursework is an Honor Code violation, and permitted use must be acknowledged. It also lists AI-generated content under plagiarism, and gives the Honor Code's sanctions and hearing standard. Instructors are urged to write a syllabus AI policy and use the pledge.
documents.stance_why: The EPC statement says 'Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor, the use of artificial intelligence ... is a violation of the Honor Code', so AI is banned unless an instructor permits it. That is restrict, not delegates, because a university default ban is set and only the exceptions are delegated.

documents.title: Wesleyan University Generative AI Usage Policy
documents.summary: ITS policy for faculty, staff, students and affiliates on using generative AI with university information. It sorts data into Public, Sensitive and Restricted and says which AI tools each may go into, and requires ITS review before AI tools are procured or integrated. It also makes users responsible for checking accuracy and copyright of AI output.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no ban: it states which data classes 'may be entered' into which AI tools, e.g. 'Only information classified as “Public” may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools', so AI use is allowed under data conditions. It says nothing on teaching stance, which it leaves to the honor code.

units.why: 'balance the innovative potential of generative AI with the need to protect sensitive information, uphold academic integrity, and comply with existing laws' states the policy's aim as an institution-wide framework; P56, all, general, informs.
units.anchor: balance the innovative potential of generative AI

units.why: 'This policy is not exhaustive, but represents work towards a thorough and comprehensive policy' says the policy is provisional; P54, all, over-time, informs.
units.anchor: This policy is not exhaustive, but represents work towards a thorough and comprehensive policy.
units.fit_note: States it is incomplete and in progress; no review cycle is named.

units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, students, and affiliates of Wesleyan University
units.fit_note: Defines scope by persons and information, not a definition of AI.

units.resolution_why: Both chose P50, all, during-work, restrict. Modality: A must-not, B must; 'Only information classified as Public may be entered' forbids every other class, so must-not.

units.why: 'If the tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as "Sensitive"' permits Sensitive data in ITS-approved tools. It binds all users while they use AI (during-work), permits (may), and is a data-protection rule tied to vetted tools (P50).

units.policy: If a generative AI tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as Sensitive into it.
units.fit_note: Permits Sensitive data in approved tools; framed as a data rule rather than a general duty to use approved tools.
units.resolution_why: A coded P92, B coded P50. The sentence is a rule about which data class may go into which tool (data protection with vetted tools), the same type both coders gave the Public and Restricted data sentences, so P50 for consistency; P92 (use approved tools) fits the approved-tool condition only partly. Both said may, permit. Both fit_notes kept.

units.policy: Information classified as Restricted cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and the relevant Cabinet member.
units.fit_note: A: Also requires named written approvers; P107 (prior approval) was not chosen because the approval concerns data, not AI use generally. B: Mainly a data rule; classed here for the named approvers and exception route.
units.resolution_why: A coded P50, B coded P80. The CISO and Cabinet member are named as approvers, but the sentence's point is a limit on what data may be entered into AI tools, not who owns or enforces the policy, so P50, matching the other data-class sentences. Both said must-not, restrict. Both fit_notes kept.
